content: The effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens may be altered by changes in intestinal flora. This interaction is relevant only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Oral neomycin reduces the effectiveness of the BCG vaccine live due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. Neomycin taken orally decreases biotin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents and is considered minor with unknown clinical significance. The combination of bumetanide and oral neomycin increases the toxicity of either drug through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction raises the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity, and alternative drugs should be considered. Oral neomycin reduces calcium acetate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents and is considered minor with unknown clinical significance. Oral neomycin decreases calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, and calcium gluconate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions are minor and apply only to oral forms of both agents, with unknown clinical significance. The combination of capreomycin and oral neomycin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Carboplatin and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Cefaclor increases the toxicity of oral neomycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefditoren, cefepime, cefepime/enmetazobactam, cefiderocol, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefpirome, cefpodoxime, cefprozil, ceftaroline, ceftazidime, ceftazidime/avibactam, ceftibuten, ceftizoxime, ceftobiprole medocaril sodium, ceftolozane/tazobactam, ceftriaxone, and cefuroxime all increase the toxicity of oral neomycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended for all these combinations. Celecoxib increases neomycin levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and mainly occurs in preterm infants, with unknown clinical significance. Cephalexin increases the toxicity of oral neomycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Cephaloridine and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated, and alternative drugs should be used. Oral neomycin reduces the effectiveness of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Cholera vaccine administration should be delayed for 14 days after oral or parenteral antibiotic use. Choline magnesium trisalicylate increases neomycin levels by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and mainly occurs in preterm infants, with unknown clinical significance. Cidofovir and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated. Oral neomycin increases the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of apnea. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Cisplatin and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Clarithromycin increases neomycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clotrimazole decreases neomycin levels through an unknown mechanism. This interaction is minor with unknown clinical significance. Colistin and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Oral neomycin decreases the levels of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Iodinated contrast media and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated. Cordyceps reduces the toxicity of oral neomycin through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is minor with unknown clinical significance. Oral neomycin decreases cyanocobalamin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents and is considered minor with unknown clinical significance. Cyclosporine increases neomycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Diclofenac, diflunisal, etodolac, fenoprofen, flurbiprofen, ibuprofen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, and ketorolac all increase neomycin levels by decreasing renal clearance. These interactions are minor and mainly occur in preterm infants, with unknown clinical significance. Fluconazole decreases neomycin levels through an unknown mechanism. This interaction is minor with unknown clinical significance. Foscarnet and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Fosphenytoin decreases neomycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Furosemide and oral neomycin both increase the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Gentamicin and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. This combination should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be used. Indinavir increases neomycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ioversol and oral neomycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated. Ketoconazole increases neomycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, ketoconazole also decreases neomycin levels through an unknown mechanism. These interactions are minor with unknown clinical significance.
